description: Anti-pattern catalog read by rig and the Reviewer. Each rule maps one detector rule to a stable AP-* ID. Every rule is advisory; none blocks. Mapping status says whether the detector rule was run (verified), taken from documentation (mapped), or does not exist yet (planned).

rules.title: Context cancel function discarded
rules.description: The cancel function returned by context.WithCancel/WithTimeout/WithDeadline is dropped or never called.
rules.rationale: The context's timer and goroutines live until the parent is cancelled: a leak per call on a hot path.
rules.remediation: Call defer cancel() immediately after creating the context.

rules.title: Lock copied by value
rules.description: A value containing a sync.Mutex (or other lock) is passed or assigned by value.
rules.rationale: The copy has its own lock state, so the code that looks synchronized is not.
rules.remediation: Pass a pointer to the struct, or keep the lock behind a pointer.

rules.title: HTTP response used before the error check
rules.description: resp.Body is deferred closed (or used) before checking the error from the request.
rules.rationale: When the request fails resp is nil, so the deferred Close panics.
rules.remediation: Check err first, then defer resp.Body.Close().

rules.title: nil passed as a context
rules.description: A function taking context.Context is called with nil.
rules.rationale: Callees that read deadlines or values from the context panic; cancellation is lost.
rules.remediation: Pass context.TODO() or, better, the caller's context.

rules.title: Error return value ignored
rules.description: A call's error result is discarded without handling.
rules.rationale: Failures continue silently and surface later, far from the cause.
rules.remediation: Handle or explicitly return the error; discard only with a comment explaining why.

rules.title: Floating promise
rules.description: A promise is created and neither awaited, returned, nor handled.
rules.rationale: Rejections are lost and ordering assumptions break; the bench's dropped-await defects are this.
rules.remediation: await it, return it, or attach an explicit .catch with handling.

rules.title: Promise passed where a void callback is expected
rules.description: An async function is used as an event handler, array callback, or condition where its promise is ignored.
rules.rationale: Errors escape the handler and code runs out of order.
rules.remediation: Wrap the call so the promise is awaited and its rejection handled.

rules.title: Explicit any
rules.description: A value is typed as any.
rules.rationale: any switches off the strict type check the playbook requires, and it spreads through inference.
rules.remediation: Use unknown and narrow it, or a precise type.

positive.code: export function parse(x: any): string { return x.name; }

rules.title: eval or new Function on runtime input
rules.description: Code is built from strings at runtime with eval.
rules.rationale: Arbitrary code execution when any part of the string is attacker-controlled; no model in the bench caught this reliably.
rules.remediation: Parse data with JSON.parse or a schema validator; never execute strings.

rules.title: Synchronous filesystem call in a server
rules.description: fs.*Sync is called in request-handling code.
rules.rationale: A sync call blocks the event loop for every concurrent request.
rules.remediation: Use the fs/promises API and await it.

rules.title: child_process with a non-literal command
rules.description: child_process.exec/spawn is called with a command built from variables.
rules.rationale: Command injection when the variable carries user input.
rules.remediation: Use execFile/spawn with a fixed command and an argument array; validate inputs.

rules.title: Peer dependency conflict forced through
rules.description: Packages with incompatible peer dependencies are installed with --force or --legacy-peer-deps, or npm ls reports invalid peers.
rules.rationale: A plugin runs against a host version it was never built for; failures appear at runtime, not install time.
rules.remediation: Pick versions whose peer ranges agree (npm ls must exit 0); never commit --legacy-peer-deps or --force.

positive.code: legacy-peer-deps=true

negative.code: engine-strict=true

rules.title: Hook called conditionally
rules.description: A React hook is called inside a condition, loop, or nested function.
rules.rationale: React matches hook state by call order; a conditional hook corrupts state between renders.
rules.remediation: Call hooks unconditionally at the top level of the component; branch inside the hook.

rules.title: Effect with missing dependencies
rules.description: useEffect/useMemo/useCallback reads values not listed in its dependency array.
rules.rationale: The effect runs with stale values and does not re-run when they change.
rules.remediation: List every reactive value the callback reads, or move it inside the effect.

rules.title: Array index used as a key
rules.description: A list is rendered with the array index as its key.
rules.rationale: Reordering or inserting items reuses the wrong component state.
rules.remediation: Use a stable ID from the data as the key.

rules.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.description: Raw HTML is injected into the DOM.
rules.rationale: Cross-site scripting when the HTML is not sanitized.
rules.remediation: Render text as children; if HTML is required, sanitize it with a vetted library first.

rules.title: Lifecycle hook called directly
rules.description: Code calls ngOnInit/ngOnDestroy (or another lifecycle method) itself.
rules.rationale: Angular calls lifecycle hooks; calling them manually runs setup or teardown twice.
rules.remediation: Move the shared logic into a private method and call that.

rules.title: Subscription never unsubscribed
rules.description: An Observable's subscribe() result is ignored in a component.
rules.rationale: The subscription outlives the component: memory leaks and handlers running on destroyed views.
rules.remediation: Use the async pipe, takeUntilDestroyed(), or keep and unsubscribe the subscription.

rules.title: Output named like a native DOM event
rules.description: An @Output() is named click, change, or another native event name.
rules.rationale: Handlers fire for both the native and the custom event.
rules.remediation: Give the output a distinct, domain-specific name.

rules.title: subprocess with shell=True
rules.description: A subprocess call runs through the shell.
rules.rationale: Command injection when any argument carries input.
rules.remediation: Pass an argument list without shell=True; validate inputs.

rules.title: Exception swallowed with pass
rules.description: except: pass (or except Exception: pass) hides every failure.
rules.rationale: Errors vanish; the bench's swallowed-error defects are this pattern.
rules.remediation: Catch the specific exception and handle or log it with context; re-raise otherwise.

rules.title: eval on runtime input
rules.description: eval() executes a string.
rules.rationale: Arbitrary code execution.
rules.remediation: Use ast.literal_eval for literals or a real parser.

positive.code:
def calc(expr):
    return eval(expr)

rules.title: HTTP request without a timeout
rules.description: requests is called without timeout=.
rules.rationale: A slow server holds the caller forever; this is ARCH-017 at the call site.
rules.remediation: Always pass timeout= (connect and read), shorter than the caller's deadline.

rules.title: yaml.load without a safe loader
rules.description: yaml.load is called without SafeLoader.
rules.rationale: Arbitrary object construction from untrusted YAML.
rules.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load.

rules.title: Mutable default argument
rules.description: A function default is a list, dict, or set.
rules.rationale: The default is shared between calls, so state leaks from one call to the next.
rules.remediation: Default to None and create the value inside the function.

negative.code:
def add(item, items=None):
    items = [] if items is None else items
    items.append(item)
    return items

rules.title: Conflicting dependencies in one environment
rules.description: Several tools or services with incompatible requirements are installed into one Python environment.
rules.rationale: The resolver fails, or worse succeeds with a broken set: one tool works and another silently runs against the wrong version.
rules.remediation: Give each tool or service its own virtualenv (or image); run pip check after every install.

positive.code:
semgrep==1.182.1
checkov==3.3.29
jsonschema==4.26.0
positive.note: Several tools with large, independent dependency trees in one environment

negative.code: jsonschema==4.26.0
negative.note: One purpose per environment; other tools in their own virtualenvs

rules.title: Raw SQL through RawSQL or extra
rules.description: Query fragments are passed to RawSQL/extra, typically built with string formatting.
rules.rationale: SQL injection, and it bypasses the ORM's parameterization.
rules.remediation: Use ORM expressions, or parameterized raw queries with params=.

negative.code:
def q(model, name):
    return model.objects.filter(name=name)

rules.title: mark_safe on dynamic content
rules.description: mark_safe() disables auto-escaping for a value.
rules.rationale: Cross-site scripting when the value contains user input.
rules.remediation: Use format_html with arguments, which escapes them.

rules.title: Nullable string field
rules.description: A CharField/TextField uses null=True.
rules.rationale: Two empty values (None and '') for one meaning; queries and code diverge.
rules.remediation: Use blank=True with default ''; reserve null for non-string fields.

rules.title: N+1 queries over a relation
rules.description: A loop over a queryset reads a related object per row without select_related/prefetch_related.
rules.rationale: One query per row; latency grows with data size. Seen in traces as repeated identical db spans under one request.
rules.remediation: Add select_related (foreign keys) or prefetch_related (many-to-many, reverse) to the queryset.

positive.code:
def names(Book):
    return [b.author.name for b in Book.objects.all()]

negative.code:
def names(Book):
    return [b.author.name for b in Book.objects.select_related('author')]

rules.title: Blocking HTTP call inside async def
rules.description: An async endpoint calls a blocking client such as requests.
rules.rationale: It blocks the event loop, so one slow call stalls every request on the worker.
rules.remediation: Use an async client (httpx.AsyncClient) or run the call in a thread pool.

negative.code:
import httpx


async def proxy(url: str):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5) as client:
        return (await client.get(url)).json()

rules.title: time.sleep inside async def
rules.description: An async function calls time.sleep.
rules.rationale: Blocks the event loop for the whole sleep.
rules.remediation: Use await asyncio.sleep().

positive.code:
import time


async def wait():
    time.sleep(1)

negative.code:
import asyncio


async def wait():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

rules.title: Dependency declared without Annotated
rules.description: A route parameter uses = Depends(...) as a default instead of Annotated.
rules.rationale: The dependency is tied to the default value, cannot be reused as a type, and breaks plain calls.
rules.remediation: Declare Annotated[T, Depends(dep)].

rules.title: SSH open to the internet
rules.description: A firewall rule allows 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22.
rules.rationale: Direct exposure of management ports; the playbook's SEC-011 and GOV-014.
rules.remediation: Restrict the source to the IAP range or a bastion; prefer OS Login through IAP.

rules.title: Basic role granted at project level
rules.description: roles/owner, roles/editor, or roles/viewer is granted on a project.
rules.rationale: Basic roles are far broader than any workload needs; the playbook's SEC-005.
rules.remediation: Grant predefined or custom roles scoped to the task.

rules.title: Publicly readable storage bucket
rules.description: allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers is granted on a bucket.
rules.rationale: Anyone can read the data; the playbook's SEC-002.
rules.remediation: Remove public members; serve public content through a CDN or signed URLs.

rules.title: Module source not pinned to a commit
rules.description: A git module source has no ref, or a branch/tag instead of a commit hash.
rules.rationale: The module can change under the same configuration: a supply-chain and reproducibility risk.
rules.remediation: Pin git sources to a full commit SHA (ref=<sha>).

rules.title: Unrestricted egress
rules.description: A firewall rule allows egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on any port.
rules.rationale: Data exfiltration and command-and-control paths are open by default.
rules.remediation: Restrict egress destinations and ports to what the workload needs; record exceptions with an owner and expiry.

rules.title: Provider without a version constraint
rules.description: A required provider has no version constraint.
rules.rationale: A provider upgrade can change behavior on the next init without any change in the code.
rules.remediation: Declare every provider in required_providers with a version constraint.

rules.title: Bare terraform invoked instead of Terragrunt
rules.description: A script or CI step runs terraform plan/apply directly in a Terragrunt repository.
rules.rationale: It bypasses the root configuration (backend, provider, inputs) and the playbook's IaC rules.
rules.remediation: Run terragrunt (or terragrunt run --all); call terraform only through it.

positive.code:
#!/bin/sh
terraform apply -auto-approve

negative.code:
#!/bin/sh
terragrunt apply

rules.title: Child unit defines its own remote_state
rules.description: A child terragrunt.hcl declares remote_state instead of including root.hcl.
rules.rationale: Backend configuration is repeated and drifts between units.
rules.remediation: Define remote_state once in root.hcl; include it from every child.

rules.title: Mock outputs usable outside plan and validate
rules.description: A dependency block sets mock_outputs without restricting them to validate/plan.
rules.rationale: An apply can run against fake values when the dependency has no state yet.
rules.remediation: Set mock_outputs_allowed_terraform_commands = ["validate", "plan"].

rules.title: Deployment unit without a class
rules.description: A unit does not declare persistent or ephemeral, or an ephemeral unit has no TTL label.
rules.rationale: Ephemeral resources without a TTL are never swept; the playbook requires a class on every unit.
rules.remediation: Declare the class in the unit's inputs/labels; give ephemeral units a TTL label.

rules.title: Reading another unit's state directly
rules.description: A module uses a terraform_remote_state data source (or reads another unit's state file) instead of a Terragrunt dependency.
rules.rationale: Hidden coupling between units that dependency ordering and plans cannot see; the playbook requires dependency blocks.
rules.remediation: Pass values through a dependency block and the other unit's outputs.

rules.title: Base image tagged latest
rules.description: FROM uses the latest tag.
rules.rationale: The image changes under the same Dockerfile; builds are not reproducible and a bad upstream push ships silently.
rules.remediation: Pin the base image to a version tag and its digest.

positive.code:
FROM python:latest
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: Container switches back to root
rules.description: The last USER instruction is root.
rules.rationale: A compromised process has root inside the container, one step from the host.
rules.remediation: End with a non-root USER (a numeric UID); do privileged setup in an earlier stage.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
RUN python -V
USER root
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER root
RUN python -V
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: No non-root user declared
rules.description: The Dockerfile never sets USER, so the container runs as root by default.
rules.rationale: Same risk as switching back to root, and the more common form of it.
rules.remediation: Create a user and set USER to its UID before CMD.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
RUN useradd --uid 10001 app
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: ADD used for local files
rules.description: ADD copies local files.
rules.rationale: ADD also fetches URLs and unpacks archives, so it does more than it says; COPY is explicit.
rules.remediation: Use COPY for files and directories.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
ADD app.py /app/app.py
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "/app/app.py"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
COPY app.py /app/app.py
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "/app/app.py"]

rules.title: Unpinned apt packages
rules.description: apt-get install runs without package versions.
rules.rationale: Each build can install different versions, so the image is not reproducible.
rules.remediation: Pin package versions, or install from a pinned base image and rebuild deliberately.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl=7.88.1-10+deb12u12 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: Pipe in RUN without pipefail
rules.description: A RUN instruction pipes commands without set -o pipefail.
rules.rationale: A failed download piped into another command still succeeds, so the build passes with a broken step.
rules.remediation: Set SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"] before piped RUN instructions.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
RUN python -V | tee /tmp/v
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]
RUN python -V | tee /tmp/v
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: Shell-form CMD or ENTRYPOINT
rules.description: CMD/ENTRYPOINT uses the shell form.
rules.rationale: The process runs under /bin/sh -c and does not receive SIGTERM, so graceful shutdown fails and the container is killed.
rules.remediation: Use the JSON (exec) form: CMD ["python", "app.py"].

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
CMD python -V

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: No HEALTHCHECK
rules.description: The image declares no HEALTHCHECK.
rules.rationale: Runtimes without their own probes cannot tell a hung process from a healthy one.
rules.remediation: Declare a HEALTHCHECK, or HEALTHCHECK NONE when the orchestrator probes the service itself.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-m", "http.server"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
USER 10001
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000')"]
CMD ["python", "-m", "http.server"]

rules.title: Secret in ENV or ARG
rules.description: A credential is set through ENV or ARG.
rules.rationale: ENV values persist in the image and ARG values in its history; anyone who can pull the image can read them.
rules.remediation: Use build secrets (RUN --mount=type=secret) at build time and a secret manager at run time.

positive.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
ENV AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc123
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

negative.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:6a0e06f5ba0b373d051aabd3fffb9b873f27f9a2a3a14bcbe37dee6f0e3bbc70
ENV APP_PORT=8000
USER 10001
CMD ["python", "-V"]

rules.title: Untrusted input expanded into a run script
rules.description: A ${{ }} expression with attacker-controlled data (PR title, branch name, issue body) is expanded inside run:.
rules.rationale: The value is pasted into the shell before it runs: script injection with the workflow's token and secrets.
rules.remediation: Pass the value through env: and reference the environment variable, quoted, in the script.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"

negative.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: echo "$TITLE"

rules.title: Action not pinned to a commit SHA
rules.description: uses: references an action by tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.
rules.rationale: A tag can be moved to malicious code; the playbook requires callers to pin by SHA.
rules.remediation: Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA, with the version in a trailing comment.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

negative.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

rules.title: Excessive workflow permissions
rules.description: A job grants write-all or broad write scopes (at the default persona, zizmor reports job-level grants; a workflow-level grant only at its pedantic persona).
rules.rationale: Every step in the job, and every action it runs, gets the broad token; the playbook defaults to contents: read.
rules.remediation: Set permissions: contents: read at the top; grant more per job, only what that job needs.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: write-all
    steps:
      - run: echo hi

negative.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - run: echo hi

rules.title: Dangerous trigger
rules.description: The workflow runs on pull_request_target or workflow_run.
rules.rationale: These run with the base repository's token and secrets while handling code or data from a fork.
rules.remediation: Use pull_request; if a privileged trigger is unavoidable, never check out or execute the fork's code.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request_target:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "labeling"

negative.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "labeling"

rules.title: Checkout persists credentials
rules.description: actions/checkout leaves the token in .git/config (persist-credentials defaults to true).
rules.rationale: Any later step, or an uploaded artifact containing .git, can read the token.
rules.remediation: Set persist-credentials: false unless a later step must push.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

name: ci
on:

permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

rules.title: Reusable workflow called with secrets: inherit
rules.description: A reusable workflow receives every secret of the caller.
rules.rationale: The callee gets far more than it needs; the playbook requires secrets to be passed explicitly.
rules.remediation: Pass each secret the callee needs by name under secrets:.

name: ci
on:

permissions:

jobs:
  gates:
    uses: org/platform/.github/workflows/gates.yml@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
    secrets: inherit

on:

permissions:

jobs:

    uses: org/platform/.github/workflows/gates.yml@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683

      token: ${{ secrets.GATES_TOKEN }}

rules.title: Expression refers to something that does not exist
rules.description: An expression references an undefined step, output, or context property, or has a type error.
rules.rationale: It evaluates to an empty string at run time, so the step silently does the wrong thing.
rules.remediation: Reference only defined step IDs and outputs; actionlint type-checks the expression.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: build
        run: echo "v=1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: echo "${{ steps.biuld.outputs.v }}"

negative.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: build
        run: echo "v=1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: echo "${{ steps.build.outputs.v }}"

rules.title: Shell bug in a run script
rules.description: A run: script has a ShellCheck finding, such as an unquoted variable.
rules.rationale: Word splitting and globbing change what the command does with unexpected input.
rules.remediation: Quote expansions and fix the ShellCheck finding; actionlint runs ShellCheck on every run: block.

positive.code:
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: rm -rf $TARGET_DIR
